target_customer: Developers and companies that embed real-time video and audio calls, and later voice AI agents, into their own products
problem: Building reliable WebRTC video and voice into an app is hard infrastructure work. Daily sells APIs and SDKs so product teams do not have to run it themselves.
business_model: usage-based API with per-minute pricing and monthly plans
product_category: real-time video and voice API, later voice AI agent infrastructure

founders.name: Kwindla Hultman Kramer
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists him as the only founder. Later he created the open-source Pipecat voice agent framework. Prior history not sourced in this pass.

founders.name: Nina Kuruvilla
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch (2021). Background not described there.

founders.name: Doug Brunton
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder only on profile pages, unverified.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable multi-party WebRTC with global media routing and low latency is hard for a small team, and the company bet on WebRTC in 2016 before it was mainstream (TechCrunch 2021 describes the 2016 founding as a bet on video, particularly WebRTC).

defensibility.rationale: Developer APIs can be replaced by rivals with similar SDKs, and customers can switch providers with integration work. Infrastructure scale gave some edge, but no strong lock-in was documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Search results show TokBox was already operating from 2010 and was bought by Vonage in 2018. No incumbent absorbed Daily. Deepgram, a fellow YC 2016 company and a long time transcription partner, announced it would acquire Daily on 2026-10-29.

market_need_then: Developers wanted to add video calling to products without running WebRTC servers. Demand jumped with the pandemic, when the company reported about 20x more paying customers and 30x more revenue in a year (TechCrunch, 2021-03).

branding.domain_note: Operates on daily.co, a country code domain. Date of acquisition not found.

identity.visual_style: Developer focused, stat callouts, bracketed uppercase section labels and slash prefixed navigation
identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and technical, short taglines, direct competitive claims

branding.brand_signature: Pipecat, the open-source voice agent framework it maintains, became the best known asset (about 17,000 GitHub stars reported at the 2026 acquisition)
branding.community_and_virality: Pipecat built a developer community and a voice agents course and community was covered in a newsletter. Pluot is reported only on profile pages.

brand_strength.rationale: A strong developer brand through open source Pipecat late in life, but the Daily name is generic and was not a documented growth driver earlier.

pivots.to: Voice and multimodal AI agent infrastructure around open source Pipecat
pivots.why: Voice AI demand. Pipecat was released in 2024 per a vendor comparison page; the pivot is described by the current website focus.

outcome_analysis: Daily bet on WebRTC in 2016, stayed small for years, then grew sharply when the pandemic drove video demand, raising a 15 million dollar Series A in March 2021 and a 40 million dollar Series B that November. It later shifted toward voice AI through the open-source Pipecat framework, which gave it a second wave of relevance. Deepgram, which went through YC in 2016 and powered Daily's transcription since 2019, announced it would acquire Daily on 2026-10-29 for an undisclosed price.
notes: Directory status says Active, but Deepgram announced the acquisition on 2026-10-29, so the exit is recorded as an announced acquisition. The 2016 seed amount is 2.5M per TechCrunch (2020) as reported by a search summary; a StartupIntros page lists 3M for August 2016, unverified. Series A lead attribution differs between outlets (Lachy Groom per TechCrunch). Total raised is over 60M per TechCrunch 2021. No competitor source dated near March 2016 was found, so the list is empty. The Pluot Communications former name and Doug Brunton appear only on profile pages, unverified. Series B investors not captured.
